- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2), model underestimates; adjust up by 1–3% if recent price is trending upward.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.0), model fails to correct; apply mean reversion bias: forecast = prior 3-day average + 0.5×(true - prior avg) for next 7 days.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts in early period (days 1–7) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; reduce first 5 days by 1–2%.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.4–0.6 range, model tends to drift upward; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for next 10 days.
